events.extended_summary: Spain has ordered olive oil mills to store 12% of production from November 2026 to regulate supply by temporarily removing oil from the market. The measure applies to monthly output reported by each mill, excluding October and earlier months, and the oil must remain off the market until 30 September 2027. Mills may use their own facilities or third-party sites. Opening stocks stand at 357,040 tonnes with production forecast at 1,602,596 tonnes. Producer prices for extra virgin olive oil have fallen to about €3 per kilo from around €4 a year earlier. The government expects 188,000 tonnes to be removed under the rule, which triggers when stocks and output exceed the six-season average by at least 20%. Spain produces about 45% of global olive oil and 70% of EU output.
events.micro_summary: Spain orders olive oil mills to store 12% of production from November 2026 to regulate supply.
events.summary: Spain has ordered olive oil mills to store 12% of their production from November 2026 until September 2027 to regulate supply, as opening stocks stood at 357,040 tonnes and production is forecast at 1,602,596 tonnes.

events.extended_summary: Te Pāti Māori won five of New Zealand's seven Māori electorate seats with only 0.56% of the party vote, creating overhang seats. Co-leaders Rawiri Waititi and Debbie Ngarewa-Packer retained Waiariki and Te Tai Hauauru, while Oriini Kaipara won Tamaki Makaurau, Hana Rawhiti Maipi-Clarke took Hauraki-Waikato, and Aperahama Edwards leads in Te Tai Tokerau. Labour claimed Te Tai Tonga with new MP Mananui Ramsden. New Zealand unemployment also reached an 11-year high, with one in three people under 24 unable to get enough work or having none at all, the worst youth job market in three decades. Young people like 20-year-old Michael Dawson report applying for dozens of jobs without interviews, while support services report unprecedented demand for employment aid.
events.micro_summary: New Zealand election yields five Te Pāti Māori seats at 0.56% vote; unemployment hits 11-year high.
events.summary: Te Pāti Māori secured five electorate seats with 0.56% party vote in New Zealand's election, while unemployment reached an 11-year high with one in three under-24s lacking adequate work.

events.extended_summary: Late night political drama as Peña is impeached and arrested Paraguay's President Santiago Peña has been impeached and placed under house arrest after a bank collapse triggered a crisis that left more than half of the country's population without access to their accounts. Peña was arrested on Friday minutes after lawmakers, including from his own party, unanimously voted to remove him from office following the collapse earlier this week of Ueno Bank, which has links to his private business interests. He had offered to step down on Thursday. Rather than accept his resignation, senators impeached Peña and charged him with misconduct, meaning he has been stripped of the immunity usually granted to ex-presidents. Peña, who until last year held shares in the company that owned the bank, has denied any wrongdoing. events.extended_summary: Pope Leo XIV is proceeding with a 12-day visit to Latin America from November 6 to 17 despite surgery last month to remove a third of his right lung after cancer was discovered. The 71-year-old will travel approximately 19,000 miles across Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru—where he served as a missionary and bishop for two decades—visiting 10 cities, taking 14 flights, delivering 36 speeches, and participating in around 50 events. The trip includes Cusco, Peru, at over 11,000 feet above sea level. Vatican officials state that while a medical team including doctors, nurses, and an ambulance will accompany him, no special precautions are being taken beyond ordinary medical assistance, as doctors confirmed there are no clinical reasons to postpone the journey. During his first day in Montevideo, Uruguay, the pope encouraged dioceses worldwide to observe days of prayer and fasting for priestly vocations, citing a local initiative that began in 2024.
events.micro_summary: Pope Leo XIV embarks on 12-day Latin America visit covering 19,000 miles despite recent lung cancer surgery.
events.summary: Pope Leo XIV is undertaking a 12-day, 19,000-mile visit to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6-17 despite recent lung cancer surgery, with a medical team accompanying him as he travels to 10 cities for 50 events.

events.extended_summary: President Donald Trump replaced White House chief of staff Susie Wiles with longtime aide Stephen Miller following the Republican Party's sweeping defeat in Tuesday's midterm elections. After initially expressing openness to collaborating with Democrats, Trump changed course amid growing agitation over the results, elevating Miller, a MAGA loyalist and architect of aggressive deportation policies. Miller, who served as deputy chief of staff for policy in Trump's second term, posted on X that the mission was to fight with all their soul to support the president. The move drew criticism from some Republicans, including Rep. Marlin Stutzman, who warned the party would remain in the minority and blamed deportation rhetoric for losing Latino voters. Wiles had co-managed Trump's successful 2024 re-election campaign. Allies argued Miller could repair the GOP's relationship with the MAGA movement, while critics viewed the selection as an extreme misread of voter rejection of Republican governance.
events.micro_summary: President Trump replaced chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller after Republican midterm losses.
events.summary: President Trump replaced White House chief of staff Susie Wiles with longtime aide Stephen Miller following Republican midterm election losses, signaling a hardline approach despite initial openness to working with Democrats.

events.extended_summary: A third wave of bomb threats targeted European airlines and media organizations this week, disrupting flights to and from Lisbon, Rome, Prague and Sofia. Three planes were escorted by Hungarian fighter jets, while nearly 30 aircraft and several airports across Europe were impacted earlier in the week. Media outlets including Ireland's public broadcaster RTÉ, the Irish Independent, NewstalkFM, TodayFM, Sky and Bulgaria's Nova TV were evacuated after receiving emailed threats from a purported "Mikhail Andropov" headlined "Message to the West". No explosives have been found on any planes. The Irish government described the situation as a "likely coordinated campaign of disruption", while European security officials are investigating whether the threats originated from pro-Kremlin activists or hacking groups. The UK characterized earlier incidents as a "malicious hoax", and a Russian extremist group denied sending the threats.
events.micro_summary: Nearly 30 aircraft and multiple media outlets faced bomb threats in Europe's third wave this week.
events.summary: A third wave of bomb threats hit European airlines and media outlets this week, forcing evacuations and fighter jet escorts for three planes, with nearly 30 aircraft impacted overall and no explosives found.

events.extended_summary: Far out in the Pacific Ocean, between Hawaii and California, a wide patch of water has been changing color over the past two decades, becoming significantly bluer and greener. It may sound inviting, but scientists have discovered there may be a disturbing reason for it: increasing plastic pollution. This part of the ocean is called the Great Pacific Garbage Patch. It’s a swirling soup of plastic trash made up of everything from old fishing nets to food and drink packaging. events.extended_summary: Global average temperatures stand approximately 1.5°C above 19th-century levels, with the first halves of 2024, 2025, and 2026 recorded as the hottest on record. The world is currently on track for 2.7°C of heating, while greenhouse gas emissions continue rising. As of early August 2026, nearly 50,000 wildfires burn globally, with over 34,000 out of control, killing approximately 1.5 million people annually. The UN has accepted that global warming will exceed 1.5°C, and scientists note the rate of warming has effectively doubled over the past decade. Researchers warn of approaching climate tipping points that could trigger cascading warming toward a Hothouse Earth scenario, potentially raising temperatures beyond any level in the past 1.2 million years and threatening industrialized civilization beyond 4°C of warming. New research suggests that as climate change worsens, political action to stop it becomes increasingly difficult.
events.micro_summary: Global temperatures have risen 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels with nearly 50,000 wildfires burning worldwide.

events.extended_summary: Kalyn Ponga returned 23 days after breaking his arm to lead New Zealand to a 34-10 victory over Tonga in the Rugby League World Cup semifinal, sending the Kiwis to their first final since 2013. The fullback contributed three try assists and a try-saving tackle on Demitric Vaimauga. New Zealand opened through Briton Nikora in the third minute. Tonga responded with two tries from Jojo Fifita to take a 10-6 lead, but Dane Gagai scored before halftime for a 12-10 New Zealand advantage. After the break, the Kiwis ran in four unanswered tries through Casey McLean, Jahrome Hughes, Xavier Willison and Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad. The match featured a pre-game stare-down following New Zealand's haka. Star prop Naufahu Whyte left with an ankle injury in the second half.

events.extended_summary: Ireland secured a dominant 42-12 victory over Argentina in the Nations Championship at Aviva Stadium in Dublin. Full-back Hugo Keenan scored a hat-trick, completing his three tries by the 50th minute, while hooker Dan Sheehan, fly-half Sam Prendergast and replacement hooker Ronan Kelleher also scored tries for the hosts. Argentina opened the scoring through wing Mateo Carreras in the 10th minute and added a second try through the same player, but were outplayed by the 55th minute. The visitors received yellow cards for centre Justo Piccardo and replacement lock Efraín Elias. Robert Baloucoune delivered an industrious display on the wing, while Robbie Henshaw, Stuart McCloskey and Mack Hansen also featured in Andy Farrell's side.
events.micro_summary: Hugo Keenan's hat-trick leads Ireland to 42-12 Nations Championship victory over Argentina.

events.extended_summary: Six-year-old Elliot English died on Friday at Children's Health Ireland hospital in Crumlin from injuries sustained in a fire on 13 October in the Birchwood area of Waterford city. The suspected arson attack also claimed the lives of his parents, Kim and Philip English, and his brothers Callum, 12, and Jayden, nine, bringing the total death toll to five family members. Another child remains in critical condition in hospital. Gardaí launched a multiple murder investigation, and while several people were arrested, most were released without charge. Jessica Dalton, 31, and Cian Stacey, 21, were remanded in custody charged with criminal damage and assault causing serious harm, with a court appearance scheduled for 17 November. The family confirmed Elliot's death with profound sadness and asked for privacy during their grief.
events.micro_summary: Six-year-old Elliot English died from fire injuries, bringing the Waterford arson death toll to five family members.

The Learjet 60 had been bound for the Bahamas from Austin, Texas when it nosedived into a multi-lane highway and exploded on impact. A tech entrepreneur and his young family, as well as the 20-year-old co-pilot, were among those who died on Sunday. The US National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) said weather conditions would be a major focus of the investigation but that it was struggling to access the wreckage due to the huge crater created by the jet on the road in Palm Beach. events.extended_summary: Paul Mackenzie's followers believed he was "Jesus's mouthpiece", the judge said last month A Kenyan court has sentenced the leader of a doomsday cult, Paul Mackenzie, to 200 years in prison for murdering 191 people, all but one of them children. Alongside 28 others, Mackenzie was found guilty of the murders for instructing members of his cult to starve their children to death so they could "meet Jesus". Justice Diana Mochache said Mackenzie bore the "primary criminal culpability" for ordering his followers to fast to death, in one of the world's deadliest episodes of cult activity. "The sentence is appropriate and just, to send an unmistakable message that such atrocities warrant the maximum penalties allowed by law," the judge added. events.extended_summary: Russian forces carried out a double-tap aerial bomb attack on Komyshuvakha in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, Ukraine, on Nov. 2, 2026. Strikes targeted an underground aid center in a school building where residents received humanitarian aid, followed by bombs hitting a shelter where people took cover. Ten guided aerial bombs were deployed, including FAB-500s and a FAB-3000 with nearly 1.5 tons of explosives and a 250-meter blast radius, collapsing the underground concrete structure. As of Nov. 6, 53 people were confirmed dead and 53 missing, while police located seven survivors, including 56-year-old Olha found unharmed on Nov. 5. Four others, including a rescue worker and a 22-year-old woman with 81% body burns, were hospitalized. Rescuers search in 15-to-20-minute intervals due to drone and bomb threats. The attack came one day after a ceasefire allowed hundreds to evacuate Russian-occupied Oleshky in neighboring Kherson Oblast.
events.micro_summary: Russian guided bombs strike Komyshuvakha, Ukraine, killing 53 and leaving 53 missing at an aid center and shelter.
events.summary: Russian forces struck an underground aid center and shelter in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia Oblast, with guided aerial bombs on Nov. 2, killing 53 people and leaving 53 missing as of Nov. 6, while rescuers search under threat of further attacks.

events.extended_summary: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings Ltd (HCCH), Indian bottling arm of The Coca-Cola Company, filed its draft red herring prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Board of India for an initial public offering. The IPO will be entirely an offer for sale of up to 99.74 crore equity shares by promoter Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings Pte. Ltd., expected to be worth around $1 billion at a $10 billion valuation. Since it is an OFS, HCCH will not receive any proceeds. The shares will be listed on the BSE and NSE. Coca-Cola owns 60% of HCCH, while Jubilant Beverages holds 40% acquired in July 2025 for ₹12,500 crore. For the quarter ended June 30, 2026, HCCH reported revenue of ₹4,310.17 crore, up 20.46% year-on-year, with sales volumes increasing 18.61% and EBITDA margin improving to 17.20%. The company operates 14 production facilities and distributes through 2,273 distributors to 1.7 million retail outlets.
events.micro_summary: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings files for $1 billion IPO offering 99.74 crore shares at $10 billion valuation.
events.summary: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings filed a draft prospectus with Sebi for an offer-for-sale IPO of up to 99.74 crore shares worth around $1 billion at a $10 billion valuation, with shares to be listed on BSE and NSE.

events.extended_summary: Priyanka Chopra Jonas announced Ventilator 2, a sequel to her 2016 Marathi production debut Ventilator, marking the 10-year anniversary of her production house Purple Pebble Pictures. The film will be produced by Chopra Jonas, Dr Madhu Chopra and Rajesh Mapuskar under Purple Pebble Pictures and Magij Pictures. Mapuskar, who wrote and directed the original, returns in the same roles. Scheduled for release in 2027, the sequel's cast, storyline and production schedule remain undisclosed. The original Ventilator, released in 2016, followed the Kamerkar family gathering at a hospital after elderly member Gajanan was placed on a ventilator, blending humour with emotional family drama. It won three National Film Awards including Best Director for Mapuskar, Best Editing and Best Sound Mixing. This production commitment is separate from Chopra Jonas's acting return in SS Rajamouli's Varanasi.

events.extended_summary: Indian businesses have moved from AI pilot projects to full-scale deployment over the past year, seeing real benefits, though cost, skills and infrastructure pose challenges, Oracle India head Shailender Kumar said. Companies want proof of time or cost savings before adopting; once tangible benefits become visible, enterprises swiftly adopt the technology. Oracle is working with universities and state governments to train students at industrial training institutes and polytechnics. Infrastructure is being addressed as new data centres come up. Governance is the most important part, requiring people to evaluate whether AI produces right outcomes, and regulation will evolve as the industry matures. Oracle, in India for 33 years across more than 15 cities, has grown at a double-digit rate for about 10 years, with banking as its biggest sector and all four telecom operators using its services. The priority for the next three to five years is faster growth.
events.micro_summary: Indian firms moved from AI pilots to full-scale deployment seeing real benefits, says Oracle India head.

events.extended_summary: India defeated New Zealand by four runs in the rain-curtailed second ODI at Wellington on Saturday, taking a 2-0 lead in the five-match series. After winning the toss and electing to bowl first, India dismissed the hosts for 134 in 41 overs, with Gurnoor Brar claiming 4/30. Chasing 135, India struggled at 47/4 before Shreyas Iyer (30) and KL Rahul (26 not out) steadied the innings. Jacob Duffy and Kyle Jamieson took 3/35 each for New Zealand. Rain interrupted play with India at 113/7, and the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method awarded India the victory by four runs as they were ahead of the par score of 109. Shubman Gill scored a duck, while Rohit Sharma made 23 and Virat Kohli 7.
events.micro_summary: India defeated New Zealand by four runs in the rain-curtailed second ODI at Wellington.
events.summary: India beat New Zealand by four runs in the rain-curtailed second ODI at Wellington, leading the series 2-0. Gurnoor Brar took 4/30 as New Zealand scored 134; KL Rahul's 26* helped India reach 113/7 before DLS confirmed the win.

events.extended_summary: India captain Shubman Gill won a delayed toss and chose to bowl Saturday in the second one-day international against New Zealand in Wellington. A wet outfield caused the toss to be delayed by an hour, and the match was reduced by rain to 47 overs per side. Both captains indicated they would bowl first in humid conditions on a pitch covered for the last two days. Both teams are unchanged from the first match in Auckland, which India won comfortably by five wickets with 56 balls remaining. That rain-affected match featured an innings of 74 by Virat Kohli, who celebrated his 38th birthday in Wellington on Thursday. India also won the previous five-match Twenty20 series 3-2. Rain fell in the morning Saturday, dampening the outfield, with heavier rain and possible thunderstorms forecast.

events.extended_summary: Mohammed Shami announced his retirement from Test cricket on Friday, ending a 12-year career that began with his debut against the West Indies at Eden Gardens on November 6, 2013. The 36-year-old fast bowler finished with 229 wickets in 67 Test matches at an average of 27.71, including six five-wicket hauls. He will continue to play white-ball cricket for India. Former cricketers Manoj Tiwary and Madan Lal paid tribute to Shami, with Tiwary calling him a "warrior" and recalling leading Bengal with him in the attack. Shami was renowned for extracting seam movement and swing with both new and old balls, with 131 of his wickets coming in 35 Tests in South Africa, the West Indies and India at an average under 25. His standout performance included a match-winning 5/28 in the 2018 Johannesburg Test.
events.micro_summary: Mohammed Shami retired from Test cricket after a 12-year career yielding 229 wickets in 67 matches.
events.summary: Mohammed Shami announced his retirement from Test cricket on Friday, concluding a 12-year international career with 229 wickets in 67 matches at an average of 27.71, while confirming he will continue playing white-ball cricket.

events.extended_summary: Three people have died following an explosion and fire at Oil India Limited's Intermediate Tank Farm in Tengakhat, Assam's Dibrugarh district. The incident occurred on Friday during maintenance work when nine workers were present at the site. Seven sustained injuries, including Raju Dutta, who died on Friday. Engineer Tapas Jyoti Gogoi, who suffered approximately 70 percent burns, died at a private hospital in Dibrugarh around 3 am on Saturday. Contractor worker Rupam Gohain of Spectron Engineering Private Limited died at a hospital in Guwahati on Saturday. Three other injured workers remain in critical condition. OIL announced an ex gratia payment of Rs 10 lakh to the next of kin of each deceased and Rs 5 lakh to each injured person. Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal and Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma are monitoring the situation.
events.micro_summary: Three people died after an explosion and fire at Oil India's Tengakhat facility in Assam.
events.summary: Three people died following an explosion and fire at Oil India's Tengakhat facility in Assam's Dibrugarh district, with two succumbing to burns on Saturday and one on Friday. Seven workers were injured, three remain critical, and OIL announced compensation.

events.extended_summary: A blast occurred at the Vasundhara police outpost in Ghaziabad district, Uttar Pradesh, on Friday night, November 6, 2026, around 9:00 p.m. The explosion damaged the window panes of the outpost, which falls under the Indirapuram police station jurisdiction. One food delivery person present at the location sustained minor injuries. A Sub-Inspector was also present at the time. On Saturday, November 7, the Bomb Disposal Squad, Field Unit, and Forensic Team gathered evidence from the site. Ghaziabad Police Commissioner J. Ravinder Goud stated that an investigation was initiated immediately and all available evidence has been collected. The cause of the explosion has not yet been revealed, and authorities are examining the incident from every possible angle. Various agencies from the Uttar Pradesh Police are involved in the thorough investigation.
events.micro_summary: A blast at a Ghaziabad police outpost injured one food delivery person on November 6, 2026.
